mainTopic: The מחלוקת between רבי יהודה and the רבנן about whether the לשכת פרהדרין (the chamber where the כהן גדול stayed before יום הכיפורים) and a סוכה need a מזוזה, and how אביי and רבא each explain that disagreement
overview: The amud opens by finishing a rejected idea. רבי יהודה cannot hold that a temporary dwelling counts as a house only מדרבנן, because that would lead people to mix up obligated and exempt produce when separating מעשרות. אביי then explains the מחלוקת about the מזוזה of the לשכת פרהדרין in a new way. Everyone agrees the chamber needs a מזוזה during the seven days the כהן גדול lives there. The only question is whether to make a גזירה for the rest of the year. רבא challenges this from the case of סוכת החג בחג, which shows the argument is about the actual days of use. So רבא says the reverse: everyone agrees the chamber is exempt the rest of the year, and the argument is about the seven days. He explains that each case has its own reason. For the סוכה, the question is whether a סוכה must be a דירת קבע or a דירת עראי. For the chamber, the question is whether a home you are forced to live in counts as a home, and רבי יהודה requires a מזוזה there only מדרבנן, so people will not say the כהן גדול is in prison. The amud ends by asking which תנא taught a ברייתא, which is quoted on the next amud.

steps.title: Why רבי יהודה cannot hold the obligation is only rabbinic
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the idea that רבי יהודה treats a temporary dwelling as a house only מדרבנן. That would cause people to separate מעשרות from obligated produce for exempt produce, or the reverse.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps he will come to separate from the obligated produce for the exempt produce, and from the exempt produce for the obligated produce.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing its rejection of an earlier suggestion. It explains the danger that would come up if a temporary dwelling were only rabbinically considered a house.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Produce that must be tithed only מדרבנן is, by Torah law, still exempt (פטור). If people cannot easily tell the Torah obligation apart from the rabbinic one, they may separate מעשרות from one kind for the other, and neither separation would work. So רבי יהודה could not have meant a merely rabbinic status, and the גמרא needs a new explanation of the מחלוקת.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps / there is a concern that
Produce that is obligated in tithing
Produce that is exempt from tithing

steps.confusionAlert: This line is the END of an argument that started on the previous amud. It is not a new topic. It explains why the previous suggestion fails, which is why אביי next says 'אלא' (rather).

phrases.english: Perhaps he will come to separate (tithes)
phrases.notes: The worry is that he'll mix up what's obligated and what isn't.

phrases.english: from the obligated (produce) for the exempt
phrases.notes: Tithes taken from Torah-obligated produce to cover produce that is exempt by Torah law

phrases.english: and from the exempt for the obligated.
phrases.notes: The reverse mistake; both separations are invalid

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the rejection of the prior (pre-passage) suggestion that רבי יהודה's view is only rabbinic
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the entire approach that explains רבי יהודה's view as a rabbinic-only house status
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A rabbinic-only status would cause confusion between obligated and exempt produce in מעשרות, leading to invalid separations

steps.title: אביי: the argument is only about the rest of the year
steps.stepSummary: אביי says everyone agrees the chamber needs a מזוזה during the seven days the כהן גדול lives there. The argument is about the rest of the year. The רבנן make a גזירה because of the seven days, and רבי יהודה does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, אביי said: During the seven days, everyone agrees the chamber is obligated. They argue about the rest of the year. The רבנן hold that we make a decree for the rest of the year because of the seven days, and רבי יהודה holds that we do not make that decree.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the previous explanation failed, אביי offers a brand-new way to understand the מחלוקת about the chamber's מזוזה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי moves the argument away from the seven days, which are not disputed at all, to the rest of the year, when nobody lives there. In his view, the only question is whether to make a גזירה so that people do not get confused. The רבנן make the גזירה and רבי יהודה does not.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (signals a new explanation replacing the old one)
The rest of the days of the year

phrases.english: Rather, Abaye said:
phrases.notes: New explanation replacing the rejected one

phrases.english: During the seven (days), everyone
phrases.notes: The seven days the כהן גדול is sequestered before יום הכיפורים

phrases.english: does not dispute that it is obligated.
phrases.notes: The chamber needs a מזוזה then

phrases.english: When they disagree is about the rest of the days of the year.
The Rabbis hold: we decree
(regarding) the rest of the year on account of the seven (days),
phrases.notes: Year-round מזוזה because of the seven days

phrases.english: and Rabbi Yehuda holds: we do not decree.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the explanation rejected in step 1 with a new framing of the מחלוקת
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-locating the dispute (shifting which time period is argued about)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The dispute was about whether a temporary dwelling counts as a house, possibly only מדרבנן
steps.terutzMaskana: Everyone agrees about the seven days; the dispute is only whether to make a גזירה for the rest of the year

steps.title: רבא challenges אביי from the case of the סוכה during the festival
steps.stepSummary: רבא objects that the source speaks of 'סוכת החג בחג', a סוכה during the festival itself. So the argument must be about the actual time of use, not the rest of the year.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: But it teaches 'the סוכה of the festival, on the festival'!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks אביי's explanation. He points to the wording of the source about the סוכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The source records a מחלוקת about a סוכה during חג itself, the time when it is actually being used. That shows the תנאים argue about the period of actual use. This contradicts אביי's claim that everyone agrees about the period of use and only argues about the rest of the year.

keyTerms.meaning: But doesn't it teach? (introduces a challenge from a source)
The סוכה of the festival, during the festival

phrases.english: Rava said to him:
But isn't it taught: 'the sukka of the festival, on the festival'?
phrases.notes: So the argument must be about the time the סוכה is actually used.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא: וְהָא סוּכַּת הֶחָג בֶּחָג קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly challenges אביי's explanation in step 2
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's claim that everyone agrees about the period of actual use
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The source explicitly places the מחלוקת during חג, the time of use, so the תנאים do argue about the period of actual use

steps.title: רבא: the argument is only about the seven days
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives the reverse explanation. Everyone agrees the chamber is exempt the rest of the year, and they argue about the seven days the כהן גדול lives there.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: During the rest of the year, everyone agrees the chamber is exempt. They argue about the seven days.
steps.whatsHappening: Because of his own challenge, רבא offers a new explanation. It is the opposite of אביי's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבא, nobody makes a year-round גזירה. The argument is about the days the place is actually lived in: the seven days for the chamber, and the festival itself for the סוכה, as the wording סוכת החג בחג shows. רבא then adds that each case turns on its own separate reason (Steps 5–7).
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two אמוראים. אביי says everyone agrees about the seven days and they argue about the rest of the year. רבא says the exact opposite: everyone agrees about the rest of the year and they argue about the seven days.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
During the rest of the days of the year
everyone agrees that it is exempt.
When they disagree is during the seven (days).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's own challenge by reversing אביי's framing
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-locating the dispute to the period of actual use
steps.terutzHavaAmina: (אביי) Everyone agrees about the seven days; the dispute is about a year-round גזירה
steps.terutzMaskana: Everyone agrees about the rest of the year (exempt); the dispute is about the seven days themselves

steps.title: The סוכה and the chamber each have their own reason
steps.stepSummary: רבא adds that the סוכה and the chamber each have a separate reason. This explains why each תנא can rule differently in the two cases without contradicting himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the סוכה has its own reason, and the chamber has its own reason.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא heads off an obvious contradiction: each side seems to rule differently for the סוכה and for the chamber. This line is a setup. The גמרא will now go on to explain what each separate reason is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under רבא's view, both cases are about a short-term dwelling. Yet the רבנן obligate the chamber and exempt the סוכה, while רבי יהודה does the reverse. רבא answers that each case is decided by its own unique reason, not by one shared rule about temporary dwellings.
steps.whatToRemember: אביי: everyone agrees the chamber needs a מזוזה during the seven days, and they argue about a year-round גזירה. רבא, after challenging this from סוכת החג בחג: everyone agrees it is exempt during the rest of the year, and they argue about the seven days. The סוכה and the chamber are each decided by their own separate reason.
steps.whyThisMatters: This line explains how each תנא can stay consistent across two similar-looking cases. It sets up the explanation of the two separate reasons that comes next.

phrases.english: And the sukka, the reason is separate,
and the chamber, the reason is separate.
phrases.notes: The chamber's ruling rests on a different reasoning, explained next

steps.triggerLanguage: וְסוּכָּה טַעְמָא לְחוּד, וְלִשְׁכָּה טַעְמָא לְחוּד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends רבא's explanation against the implied contradiction between the סוכה and chamber rulings
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases (each has an independent reason)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The סוכה and the chamber should follow the same rule, since both are short-term dwellings
steps.terutzMaskana: Each case is decided by its own reason, so the different rulings are not contradictory

steps.title: The separate reason for the סוכה
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains the סוכה dispute. רבי יהודה requires a סוכה to be a דירת קבע, so it needs a מזוזה. The רבנן require a דירת עראי, so it is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: The סוכה has its own reason. רבי יהודה follows his own view, since he says a סוכה must be a permanent dwelling, and so it is obligated in מזוזה. The רבנן follow their own view, since they say a סוכה must be a temporary dwelling, and so it is not obligated in מזוזה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא now fills in the first half of his claim that each case has its own reason. He shows that the argument about the סוכה comes from a separate, well-known dispute about what kind of structure a סוכה must be.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מזוזה ruling for the סוכה is not about time of use or forced dwelling. It follows from each side's definition of a סוכה. If a סוכה must be like a real house (רבי יהודה), it gets a house's מזוזה. If it must be temporary (רבנן), it does not.

keyTerms.meaning: A separate reason; this case has its own logic

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up who is strict here. On the סוכה, רבי יהודה is the one who requires a מזוזה, because he sees a סוכה as a permanent dwelling. The רבנן exempt it.

phrases.english: The sukkah has a separate reason —
Rabbi Yehuda follows his own view, for he said:
For a sukkah we require a permanent dwelling,
phrases.notes: רבי יהודה's well-known position on סוכה requirements

phrases.english: and so it is obligated in mezuzah.
And the Rabbis follow their own view, for they say:
For a sukkah we require a temporary dwelling,
and so it is not obligated in mezuzah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the סוכה half of רבא's statement in Step 5 that each case has its own reason.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Separate underlying reasoning (each ruling is rooted in a different dispute)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might think each תנא's rulings on the סוכה and the לשכה should match, so ruling differently looks like a contradiction.
steps.terutzMaskana: The סוכה ruling depends only on whether a סוכה must be דירת קבע or דירת עראי, so it does not have to match the chamber ruling.

steps.title: The separate reason for the chamber
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains the chamber dispute. The רבנן hold that a forced dwelling still counts as a dwelling. רבי יהודה holds it does not, and its מזוזה is only מדרבנן, so people will not say the כהן גדול is imprisoned.
steps.simpleTranslation: The chamber also has its own reason. The רבנן hold that a dwelling you live in against your will is still called a dwelling. רבי יהודה holds that such a dwelling is not called a dwelling. It was the חכמים who made a rule to put a מזוזה there, so that people will not say: the כהן גדול is locked up in a jail.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא now explains the second half of his claim. He shows that the chamber dispute has nothing to do with what a סוכה must be. It depends on whether a place you are forced to live in counts as a real home.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כהן גדול lives in the לשכת פרהדרין because the law requires it, not by choice. The רבנן still call it a home, so it needs a מזוזה. רבי יהודה says a forced home is not a real home, so by Torah law there is no obligation. He agrees to a מזוזה only as a rabbinic rule, so that the place will not look like a prison, which has no מזוזה.

keyTerms.meaning: A chamber in the בית המקדש (here, the לשכת פרהדרין where the כהן גדול stays for seven days)
A dwelling one lives in against one's will (by force or obligation)
It is called a dwelling (it has the legal status of a home)

steps.whatToRemember: רבא's full answer: each תנא's two rulings come from two different issues. The סוכה depends on whether a סוכה must be permanent or temporary. The chamber depends on whether a forced dwelling counts as a home. So רבי יהודה can require a מזוזה for a סוכה by Torah law and still say the chamber needs one only מדרבנן. The רבנן can exempt a סוכה and still treat the chamber as a real home.
steps.confusionAlert: On the chamber, the sides flip compared to the סוכה. Here it is the רבנן who treat it as a real home. רבי יהודה says it is not one by Torah law and requires a מזוזה only מדרבנן. That flip is exactly why רבא needed separate reasons.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common method in the גמרא. An apparent contradiction in a תנא's rulings disappears once you show the two rulings rest on different principles.

phrases.english: And the chamber has a separate reason:
The Rabbis hold:
A dwelling lived in against one's will is called a dwelling.
And Rabbi Yehuda holds:

phrases.aramaic: דִּירָה בְּעַל כׇּרְחָהּ לֹא שְׁמָהּ דִּירָה,
phrases.english: A dwelling lived in against one's will is not called a dwelling,
and it is by rabbinic law that they instituted it (the mezuzah),
so that people will not say:
The High Priest is locked up in a prison.
phrases.notes: A prison has no מזוזה, so a doorway without one would make the chamber look like a jail.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבא's explanation by giving the chamber's separate reason, the pair to the סוכה reason in Step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Separate underlying reasoning (each ruling is rooted in a different dispute)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since רבי יהודה treats a סוכה as a permanent home needing a מזוזה, one would expect him to require a מזוזה in the chamber by Torah law too.
steps.terutzMaskana: The chamber question is about forced dwelling. רבי יהודה says a forced dwelling is not a home, so its מזוזה is only a rabbinic rule to avoid the look of a prison.

steps.title: Which תנא taught the following ברייתא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a new question, asking which תנא is behind a ברייתא that it is about to quote.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who is the תנא who taught this, as the חכמים taught in a ברייתא:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It asks who the author of a certain ברייתא is, and the ברייתא itself will be quoted right on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The formula מאן תנא asks which known opinion a teaching follows. Here it introduces a ברייתא that the גמרא will try to match to רבי יהודה or the רבנן. Nothing is decided yet; this line only opens the inquiry.

keyTerms.meaning: Who taught this? (asking which תנא is the author of a teaching)
The חכמים taught (the standard opening for a ברייתא)

phrases.english: Who is the tanna who taught this
that the Sages taught in a baraita:
phrases.notes: The ברייתא itself appears on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing רבא's explanation, the גמרא starts a new inquiry into who authored a related ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The identity of the תנא whose opinion is reflected in the ברייתא about to be quoted.
